notable.name: Quechua
notable.note: co-official in areas where it predominates (Art. 48 of the Constitution); Peru was the first country to recognize Quechua as official, in 1975

notable.name: Aymara
notable.note: co-official in areas where it predominates

terrainDescription.zh: 西部為狹長沙漠海岸，中部安地斯山脈縱貫全國，東部則降入亞馬遜雨林盆地——三種截然不同的地形帶並存。
terrainDescription.en: A narrow desert coastline in the west, the Andes running through the center, and Amazon rainforest lowlands in the east — three starkly different terrain bands in one country.

roadInfra.bollardStyle: "Cigarette"-shaped bollards, sometimes with black stripes; sign posts are distinctively black-and-white striped and often set into a raised solid-concrete base — one of Peru's most reliable visual clues

utilityPole.transformerMount: Poles distinguished by three arms extending outward from the shaft

historicalContext.zh: 西班牙語為全國官方語言，但根據憲法第48條，克丘亞語與艾馬拉語在其主要分布地區具共同官方地位；秘魯也是1975年全球第一個將克丘亞語列為官方語言的國家。
historicalContext.en: Spanish is the national official language, but Quechua and Aymara are co-official in the areas where they predominate under Article 48 of the Constitution; Peru was also the first country in the world to recognize Quechua as an official language, in 1975.
